summary: Repaired `bin/copy-image`. Copies now preserve sparse holes, use atomic replacement for safe reruns, and survive node restart. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced the `cat`-based implementation with a POSIX-shell wrapper around the installed `cp --sparse=always`.
Added argument validation, same-file protection, temporary-file cleanup, and atomic destination replacement.
Restarted node1 safely and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Sparse, byte-exact 64 MiB copy under 2 MiB allocated
evidence.summary: Source and destination hashes match; both are 67,108,864 logical bytes, while the destination occupies only 20,480 bytes.
A second copy succeeded via atomic replacement, remained sparse and identical, and left no temporary directories.
Same-file copying was rejected; the source hash and inode remained unchanged.
The existing coreutils 5.97 supports sparse copying; the repaired executable passes `/bin/sh` syntax validation.

Healthy baseline boot ID `a7a2cfcf-5a20-4268-8000-000000000000` was captured, restart acknowledged, and new boot ID `d7afb2e2-74bb-4323-8000-000000000000` proved a node restart. SSH, source data, repaired utility, sparse destination, and repeated copying all recovered successfully.
